title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months of His Life for One Film. This Is What Obsession Looks Like.
excerpt: From wrapping Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War straight into a six-month physical transformation for Parashurama — Mahavatar is the most ambitious bet any Bollywood star has made in years.
body:
There is a version of a Bollywood career where you do four films a year, show up looking roughly the same in each one, and let the box office sort it out. **Vicky Kaushal** has apparently decided that version is not for him.

According to an exclusive report by *Pinkvilla*, Kaushal has blocked a staggering 18 months — from mid-2026 through the end of 2027 — exclusively for **Mahavatar**, the Maddock Films mythological epic in which he will portray **Chiranjeevi Parashurama**, the immortal sage-warrior and sixth avatar of Vishnu. No side projects. No brand shoots squeezed in between schedules. Just one man, one role, and the kind of commitment Bollywood hasn't seen since Aamir Khan vanished into *Dangal*.

## From Bhansali's Set Straight Into the Fire

The timeline is almost comically intense. Kaushal is currently deep in the final stretch of **Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War**, the sweeping drama that also stars **Ranbir Kapoor** and **Alia Bhatt**. Bhansali kicked off a crucial 50-day schedule in May 2026 and is aiming to wrap by the end of June, targeting a theatrical release on **January 21, 2027**.

The moment Love and War wraps, Vicky doesn't take a holiday. He walks straight into a six-month preparatory module designed by director **Amar Kaushik** — the man behind the *Stree* franchise and *Munjya*, who has quietly become one of Indian cinema's most bankable filmmakers.

> "The prep is going on for 6-7 months. We have worked on the set design, weapon design, how every character would look. The scripting is done. Yet, we need more time." — Amar Kaushik

## The Transformation

This isn't a casual workshop period. The preparatory phase includes a **rigorous physical transformation** — Kaushik has designed a detailed module aimed at bulking Kaushal's physique to match the mythological scale of Parashurama, a figure known in Hindu tradition for immense strength, spiritual depth, and an axe that could split mountains. Alongside the body work, Kaushal will undergo intensive acting workshops focused on the psychological and emotional architecture of the character.

The first-look poster, released months ago, already showed a **fierce, nearly unrecognizable Vicky** — all sinew and fury, a world away from the charming lover of *Masaan* or the roguish husband of *Bad Newz*. If the final product delivers on that promise, we're looking at a career-defining transformation.

Actual filming begins in **January 2027** and is expected to run through **December 2027** — a full year of principal photography. During this entire window, Kaushal has reportedly decided not to accept any other professional commitments.

## Shraddha Kapoor May Join the Epic

As if the project needed more star power, *Mid-Day* reports that **Shraddha Kapoor** is in advanced talks to play the female lead. If signed, it would mark the first on-screen pairing of two of Bollywood's biggest box office draws — a combination the makers believe could add serious heat to an already scorching project.

Shraddha, coming off her own run of blockbusters including *Stree 2*, fits the brief perfectly according to insiders. The makers wanted someone who brings both star value and screen presence, and few names in the industry check both boxes as convincingly as she does.

## What It Means for Bollywood

Mahavatar represents a bold new direction for Maddock Films, which built its recent empire on the horror-comedy universe of *Stree*, *Bhediya*, and *Munjya*. Moving into large-scale mythological territory is a significant gamble — but with Kaushik directing and Kaushal giving up a year and a half of his career, it's a gamble backed by total conviction.

For the diaspora audience, the project signals something exciting: Indian cinema is entering its myth-making era. Between Ranbir Kapoor's **Ramayana**, Ranveer Singh's ₹300 crore zombie epic **Pralay**, and now Kaushal's Parashurama — Bollywood is no longer just competing with Hollywood blockbusters. It's building its own cinematic universes rooted in Indian mythology.

Mahavatar was originally slated for Christmas 2026 but has been pushed to **2027** — likely the Independence Day weekend, though that would put it on a collision course with Maddock's own *Stree 3*. Either way, when it arrives, it won't be just another film. It'll be the result of 18 months of one man's total surrender to a role.

And if that poster is anything to go by, Vicky Kaushal is going to make us forget he was ever anyone else.
